title: Stopping a monster without killing it
summary: R.E.P.O. gives you ways to stop a monster rather than destroy it: the game ships a stun baton, stun grenades and stun mines, and a monster that has been stunned runs on its own recovery timer.
body: Not every tool is meant to kill. The game ships weapons built to stun, so a crew can buy itself time without having to win the fight that time is meant to avoid.
There is more than one way to deliver it. A baton is held, a grenade is thrown and a mine is left behind, so the same idea reaches a monster by three quite different routes.
Being stunned is a state of its own. A stunned monster runs on a timer with a defined start and end, which is why a stun is a window you have to use rather than a permanent answer.
Mines are not all the same object. The game sorts them into kinds covering explosive, shockwave and stun, so what you set down is a deliberate choice rather than one generic trap.

A mine also has to be armed. A placed mine arms and then triggers, and it can be told whether enemies, players, thrown objects or plain forces set it off, which is why a badly placed mine becomes your own problem.

Explosives are a separate family again. Grenades tick before they go off and some of them are specialised, so the line between stopping a monster and destroying the loot you came for is one you choose.
What this entry does not tell you: how long a stun lasts, what any of it costs, or how much damage a blast does. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The game ships a baton built to stun.
Stun grenades and stun mines exist as items of their own.
A stunned monster runs on a timer with a defined start and end.
Mines are sorted into kinds, covering explosive, shockwave and stun.
A placed mine arms and then triggers, and can choose what sets it off.
